methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $500M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Wandelbots is a Series G robotics and manufacturing automation company that has raised $126M to date. The valuation universe comprises ten Robotics & Manufacturing peers: one public company (277810.KQ) and nine private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to support a reliable peer-median approach; only one adjacent-stage peer exists within the filtered criteria, below the three-datapoint threshold needed for robust triangulation.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($126M) as a baseline proxy normalized to $500M, and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement, this method yields a $625M implied valuation. This serves as the median anchor for the range.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $531M to $719M, centered on $625M. This range reflects approximately ±15% variance around the median to account for single-method dependency and execution risk. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer comparables, which limits cross-validation against similarly-staged frontier robotics companies, and undisclosed current fundraising terms or post-money documentation. The valuation relies heavily on stage-progression mechanics rather than market multiples, warranting reassessment once additional same-stage private or public robotics peers reach comparable maturity or liquidity events.
